brief: This week 14 new startups joined the list, bringing the total tracked to 50 companies worth watching. The strongest newcomer is TEKEVER, a Portuguese company building autonomous drones and software that fly missions and gather intelligence for armies and border agencies without risking pilots, and it stands out because proving its technology in a real conflict has kept investors funding it at higher and higher prices. The trend of the week is cybersecurity rebuilt for the AI and cloud era, with newcomers like Island, Cyera and Upwind building tools to see and stop threats where old security tools no longer reach.
gaps: Almost every startup here is European, North American or Israeli, with barq the lone entry from the Middle East and none at all from Latin America or Sub-Saharan Africa; barq's licensed digital-wallet model for cross-border payments looks very exportable to those underserved regions.

AI is already drafting notes for doctors (Tandem Health, Nabla, Epsilon Health) and lawyers (Lawhive, Lexroom), but nobody in this batch targets the paperwork and diagnosis burden of caring for the aging population, even though the same listen-and-draft trick could serve home care workers and nursing homes.

Robotics entries like Maven Robotics and Dexory pick 'the ugliest job' in a warehouse, and Foxglove and FYLD tame the data construction and robotics teams produce, but nobody builds the physical robot for the ugliest jobs on a construction site itself, like drywall, cleanup or bricklaying.

The commercial space cluster (The Exploration Company, Open Cosmos, Kepler Aerospace, MBRYONICS, Hubble Network) is entirely about getting satellites up and talking to each other, leaving a gap for in-orbit servicing or debris removal as that satellite population keeps growing.

Endra automates the design paperwork for a building's mechanical and electrical systems, but the actual electricians, plumbers and HVAC technicians doing the physical trade work in the field still lack an AI copilot for diagnosis and dispatch, unlike the frontline-worker focus Sona brings to scheduling.
run_line: 65 searches of 250, 102 pages of 200, 51 startups judged of 60, 96 minutes

title: Hot Startups

trends.name: AI accelerates scientific discovery
trends.sentence: Startups are pointing generative AI and machine learning at slow, expensive lab work to design drugs, proteins, materials and engineering simulations far faster than trial-and-error.

trends.name: Cybersecurity rebuilt for the AI and cloud era
trends.sentence: As AI agents, cloud workloads and firmware create new attack surfaces, a wave of startups is rebuilding security tools to see and stop threats where the old tools no longer reach.

trends.name: Autonomous AI agents replace knowledge work
trends.sentence: Once AI models could reliably finish multi-step tasks, startups packaged them as agents that do an entire job end to end, from coding and selling to recruiting and workflow automation.

trends.name: Picks-and-shovels for the AI compute boom
trends.sentence: Instead of building AI models, these startups sell the chips, chip-to-chip interconnects, networking, data centers and inference APIs that everyone building AI needs.

trends.name: A new commercial space race
trends.sentence: Startups are building reusable capsules, small satellites, optical laser links and satellite networks that tap existing chips, making space access and communication cheaper and faster to deploy.

trends.name: AI voice agents that talk like humans
trends.sentence: Once text-to-speech and conversational AI crossed a quality bar, startups wrapped it into voice agents that tutor, chat, animate avatars and handle real phone calls for businesses.
